title: Adaptive Markets and the 2008 coordination failure
summary: Lo's three-body market frame applied to 2008: rational models created complex, opaque instruments; herding drove their adoption and mispricing; fragile market structure amplified the shock. The three coordinated destructively into systemic collapse.
source: Ch04 — "Trading: Where Coordination Becomes Visible" (Lo, Raschke)

nodes.label: Rational Models
nodes.description: Statistical models, AAA ratings, diversification logic

nodes.label: Opaque Instruments
nodes.description: CDOs and MBS whose risk almost nobody understood

nodes.label: Behavioral Herding
nodes.description: Fear of missing out, overconfidence, "prices never fall"

edges.description: Rational models engineered complex, opaque instruments
Herding drove adoption and mispricing of the instruments
AAA ratings and apparent returns legitimised more herding
Opaque, correlated exposure turned a housing shock into a systemic one
Weak, interconnected structure amplified the shock

identifiability_note: Models, psychology and structure co-moved throughout the cycle; without an unshocked control economy the contribution of each body is not separable.
